page: OVHcloud r2-60-flex is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Haswell architecture processor operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz across 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores, with one thread per core and hyper-threading disabled. The CPU cache layout provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AES cryptographic acceleration, BMI2, and FMA. Hardware configuration includes 60 GB of system memory, yielding a generous 15 GB of RAM per vCPU, paired with 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage. No discrete GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

Standard synthetic and practical benchmarks reflect the legacy microarchitecture of the host CPU. On stress-ng, the instance achieves 1027.68 in single-core performance and 4074.47 in multi-core metrics. Geekbench scoring indicates 682.0 for single-core tasks and 2116.0 for multi-core processing, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3977.41 and a PassMark memory rating of 1616.21. In memory throughput testing, uncached large-block write operations reach 33.02 GB/sec, placing it in mid-tier performance, whereas uncached large-block read operations register at 33.67 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 2.19 million operations per second, while static web serving achieves 3.51 GB/sec.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the r2-60-flex offers substantial memory capacity relative to compute allocation, allowing applications with large resident working sets to function without over-provisioning processing cores. However, users face lower computational throughput and compression performance due to older CPU execution units and the absence of modern vector instruction sets like AVX-512. The instance is well suited for memory-intensive workloads that tolerate moderate processor speeds, such as in-memory caches, distributed message buffers, staging databases, and background ETL batch jobs.
description: OVHcloud r2-60-flex is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Haswell processor on KVM virtualization. The configuration delivers 4 dedicated x86_64 physical cores clocked at 2.2 GHz alongside 60 GB of RAM, establishing an expansive 15 GB of memory per core. Bundled storage includes a 50 GB local SSD, while no dedicated graphics accelerators are included. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread and multi-thread computational capacity, with a Geekbench single-core score of 682.0 and a multi-core score of 2116.0, reflecting the older architectural generation. PassMark memory and database evaluations also position raw throughput in lower comparative tiers, though write memory bandwidth reaches 33.02 GB/sec. Because the instance pairs high RAM density with legacy CPU execution, it serves as an economical resource profile for memory-bound tasks that do not demand cutting-edge processor throughput. Suitable deployments include in-memory key-value caches, intermediate data buffers, staging databases, and memory-intensive batch processing.
